long_description.before: Skillsync is an AI recruiter that hires engineers based on what they've shipped. The best engineers are not on LinkedIn. They're on GitHub, busy shipping code. But GitHub is massive, chaotic, and nobody had made it searchable for hiring. Skillsync changes that. Companies search directly for capabilities and we surface engineers already building in their domain. Companies like Ramp, Bun, and Zed use Skillsync to hire for critical roles, with Bun seeing 5x improvement in conversion rates. We're starting with open source and expanding to research papers, private repos, and every surface where real work happens. We're building the LinkedIn for the AI era
long_description.after:
Skillsync is a real-time multiplayer coding agent with shared memory. Teams build with coding agents together, live, in the terminal or a Discord-like app, then every session becomes searchable memory the whole team and its agents can reuse.

Today, all the thinking behind your code lives inside individual agent sessions and evaporates the moment they close. The reasoning, what was tried, what was rejected, the taste that sets your best engineers apart, just becomes tribal knowledge stuck in a few heads. Skillsync captures it. We're formalizing engineering culture, so how your team uniquely builds becomes explicit, shared, and reusable.

one_liner.before: Hire engineers based on what they’ve shipped

one_liner.after: Give your company the knowledge it deserves

long_description.before:
Geopolitical conflicts (US-Iran war) and natural disasters (Winter Storm Uri) consistently expose the vulnerability of the US chemical industry. The reason? Production is centralized and fossil fuel-dependent. The solution? Domestic biogas: The US produces enough biogas to make over $20 bn/y worth of chemicals, but 60% is wasted in low-margin applications or flared altogether. 

Rise Reforming is commercializing a modular process to transform this underutilized biogas on-site into cheap, supply-secure chemicals. Our beachhead market is dimethyl ether (DME), used as an aerosol propellant and a low-carbon fuel additive in propane. Our target market is methanol: an established billion $ chemical and the future of low-carbon shipping.
